title: Can we change the order of the terms to add quickly?
description: A long sum is worked out quickly by changing the order of its terms and putting some of them together, and a shorter sum is worked out the same way. Keeko doubts that the minus sign covers both the numbers after it.
teaching_notes: One idea: a term keeps its own sign when it moves, so terms can be swapped and grouped to make easy sums. Watch for students who think a minus sign covers every number that follows it.

source: Evaluate 83 + 28 − 13 + 32 by swapping and grouping, and the
video_script.why: A learner sees that terms can be moved with their own signs and grouped, so that a long sum becomes easy to work out.
video_script.substitution: The book's own sum of four terms, and then the shorter sum of three terms.
video_script.anchor: a long sum whose terms can be swapped and grouped
video_script.wrong_answer: thirty four minus fourteen plus twenty is thirty four minus thirty four
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko takes 14 and 20 away together, so 34 minus 34 gives 0, but the minus belongs only to the 14 and the value is 40.
video_script.payoff_line: The first sum is one hundred and thirty, and the second is forty

final_answer.spoken: the values are one hundred and thirty and forty

never_show: the two values together before the answer beat
video_script.design: One idea: terms keep their signs when they move, so they can be swapped and grouped. Assumes terms of an expression. The number tiles stay on the stage and move with their signs. Wrong idea: the minus covers all the numbers after it.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a long sum of four numbers on a card, and a shorter sum of three numbers on a second card

marks.p1: the title card From your book arrives
marks.p2: a long sum of four numbers appears on a card
marks.p3: a shorter sum of three numbers appears on a second card
marks.p4: a question mark glows over the two cards

narration: <bookmark mark='p1'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='p2'/>It gives a long sum with four numbers, some added and one taken away.
<bookmark mark='p3'/>The book also gives a shorter sum with three numbers.
<bookmark mark='p4'/>How can we make a sum like this quick to work out?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: number tiles 83, 28, −13 and 32 in a row; two tiles trade places, then two tiles sit inside a bracket; the minus stays on its tile

marks.g1: two tiles trade places in the row
marks.g2: two tiles are put inside a bracket
marks.g3: the minus sign is shown glued to the tile for 13 as it moves

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>Changing the order of the terms is called swapping.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>Putting some of the terms together in brackets is called grouping.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>A term keeps its own sign when it moves, so the minus stays with its number.

marks.gv2: the shorter sum is written under it

narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, the long sum is eighty three plus twenty eight minus thirteen plus thirty two.
<bookmark mark='gv2'/>The shorter sum is thirty four minus fourteen plus twenty.

beats.on_screen: To find: the value of each sum, by swapping and grouping
narration: <bookmark mark='fd1'/>We find the value of each sum by swapping and grouping.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the terms of 83 + 28 − 13 + 32 are 83, 28, −13 and 32

marks.s1a: the four terms are circled one by one
marks.s1b: the minus sign is joined to the term 13

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>The terms are eighty three, twenty eight, minus thirteen and thirty two.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>The minus belongs to the thirteen only.

marks.s2a: the tile for −13 moves next to the tile for 83
marks.s2b: brackets are put round 83 − 13 and round 28 + 32

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Swap the terms so that eighty three is next to minus thirteen.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>Group eighty three with minus thirteen, and twenty eight with thirty two.
<bookmark mark='s3a'/>Eighty three minus thirteen is seventy, and twenty eight plus thirty two is sixty.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>Seventy plus sixty is one hundred and thirty.
<bookmark mark='s4a'/>In the second sum, the terms are thirty four, minus fourteen and twenty.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>Thirty four minus fourteen is twenty, and twenty plus twenty is forty.

marks.ans: the two values are boxed together

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The first sum is one hundred and thirty, and the second is forty.
Swapping and grouping made each sum quick to work out.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 34 − 14 + 20 = 34 − 34, struck out ; the correct working 34 − 14 = 20, then 20 + 20 = 40

marks.d2: 34 − 34 = 0 is written in the bubble and a bracket is drawn round 14 + 20
marks.d3: the bubble is struck out and the correct working is written beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='d1'/>Keeko thinks thirty four minus fourteen plus twenty is thirty four minus thirty four. The minus is thought to cover both.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>That would give zero, but the minus belongs only to the fourteen.
<bookmark mark='d3'/>Thirty four minus fourteen is twenty, and then twenty is added, which gives forty.
